001package io.jstach.rainbowgum;
002
003import java.io.PrintStream;
004import java.lang.System.Logger.Level;
005import java.time.Instant;
006import java.util.ArrayList;
007import java.util.Arrays;
008import java.util.List;
009import java.util.Locale;
010import java.util.Map;
011import java.util.Objects;
012import java.util.concurrent.CopyOnWriteArrayList;
013import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicLong;
014import java.util.concurrent.locks.ReentrantLock;
015import java.util.function.Supplier;
016
017import org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable;
018
019import io.jstach.rainbowgum.annotation.EnumAlias;
020
021/**
022 * Alerts (sometimes called errors or status events elsewhere) are for reporting problems
023 * with the logging system itself rather than application logging - for example an
024 * appender failing to write, or an async publisher's queue overflowing. Because logging
025 * itself may be broken these are not routed through the normal {@link LogRouter} but are
026 * instead kept in a small in memory ring buffer (see {@link #dump()} and
027 * {@link #stats()}). Warning and error alerts are also reported immediately (currently to
028 * stderr); informational alerts remain available for diagnostics without producing output
029 * by default.
030 * <p>
031 * An instance is available from every {@link LogConfig#alerts()}. Components that are
032 * {@linkplain LogProvider provided} config, or that are
033 * {@linkplain LogLifecycle#start( LogConfig) started} with config, should prefer
034 * capturing {@code config.alerts()} over reaching for global state.
035 * <p>
036 * {@link LogAlerts} is itself a {@link LogLifecycle}: {@link #start(LogConfig)} is called
037 * exactly once, after every
038 * {@link io.jstach.rainbowgum.spi.RainbowGumServiceProvider.Configurator} has run, and is
039 * where {@link UnobservedErrorsAction} (already resolved at construction, same as
040 * capacity) gets applied against whatever has been recorded by then - see that enum for
041 * what "nobody is listening yet" means and why it matters specifically at that moment
042 * rather than for the life of the process.
043 *
044 * @see LogConfig#alerts()
045 */
046public sealed interface LogAlerts extends LogLifecycle permits DefaultLogAlerts, SwappableLogAlerts {
047
048        /**
049         * Default capacity of the alert ring buffer.
050         */
051        static final int DEFAULT_CAPACITY = 512;
052
053        /**
054         * Key of the key value, set to {@code true}, that marks an alert as being about
055         * configuration, such as a property key that was set but not read. Only those alerts
056         * fail startup with {@link FailLevel#CONFIG}. See
057         * {@link #config(Class, Level, String, Throwable)}.
058         */
059        static final String CONFIG_KEY = "alert.config";
060
061        /**
062         * Records an alert.
063         * @param event event describing the alert.
064         */
065        public void alert(LogEvent event);
066
067        /**
068         * Records an alert.
069         * @param loggerName usually the class where the alert originated.
070         * @param throwable cause of the alert.
071         */
072        default void error(Class<?> loggerName, Throwable throwable) {
073                String m = Objects.requireNonNullElse(throwable.getMessage(), "exception");
074                error(loggerName, m, throwable);
075        }
076
077        /**
078         * Records an alert.
079         * @param loggerName usually the class where the alert originated.
080         * @param message alert message.
081         * @param throwable cause of the alert.
082         */
083        default void error(Class<?> loggerName, String message, Throwable throwable) {
084                alert(event(loggerName, Level.ERROR, message, throwable));
085        }
086
087        /**
088         * Records an alert about configuration, such as a property that is set wrong, as
089         * opposed to a problem while logging, such as an appender failing to write.
090         * Configuration sources outside core use it so {@link FailLevel#CONFIG} can fail
091         * startup on their alerts.
092         * @param loggerName usually the class where the alert originated.
093         * @param level alert level.
094         * @param message alert message.
095         * @param throwable cause of the alert, if any.
096         * @see #CONFIG_KEY
097         */
098        default void config(Class<?> loggerName, Level level, String message, @Nullable Throwable throwable) {
099                var currentThread = Thread.currentThread();
100                alert(LogEvent.of(Instant.now(), currentThread.getName(), currentThread.threadId(), level, loggerName.getName(),
101                                message, DefaultLogAlerts.configKeyValues(), throwable));
102        }
103
104        /**
105         * Records a warning alert.
106         * @param loggerName usually the class where the alert originated.
107         * @param message alert message.
108         */
109        default void warn(Class<?> loggerName, String message) {
110                alert(event(loggerName, Level.WARNING, message, null));
111        }
112
113        /**
114         * Records an informational alert.
115         * @param loggerName usually the class where the alert originated.
116         * @param message alert message.
117         */
118        default void info(Class<?> loggerName, String message) {
119                alert(event(loggerName, Level.INFO, message, null));
120        }
121
122        private static LogEvent event(Class<?> loggerName, Level level, String message, @Nullable Throwable throwable) {
123                var currentThread = Thread.currentThread();
124                return LogEvent.of(Instant.now(), currentThread.getName(), currentThread.threadId(), level,
125                                loggerName.getName(), message, KeyValues.of(), throwable);
126        }
127
128        /**
129         * A snapshot of the alerts currently held in the ring buffer, oldest first. Alerts
130         * are evicted oldest first once the buffer is at {@link Stats#capacity()}.
131         * @return immutable snapshot.
132         */
133        public List<LogEvent> dump();
134
135        /**
136         * Clears the ring buffer. Does not reset {@link Stats#total()} - like a
137         * Prometheus/Micrometer counter, that is meant to be monotonically increasing for the
138         * life of the process; a downstream metrics system computes rate of change rather
139         * than relying on the counter itself being reset. Clearing diagnostics does not undo
140         * an alert that fails startup under {@link FailLevel}.
141         */
142        public void clear();
143
144        /**
145         * Stats about the alerts recorded so far.
146         * @return stats.
147         */
148        public Stats stats();
149
150        /**
151         * Registers a listener that is notified synchronously, in addition to the alert being
152         * recorded in the ring buffer, every time {@link #alert(LogEvent)} is called.
153         * <p>
154         * <strong>Listeners are held with a normal (strong) reference and are not
155         * automatically removed.</strong> This is deliberate: alert listeners are expected to
156         * be few and long lived - typically registered once (e.g. a metrics bridge or an
157         * ops/paging integration) for as long as the owning {@link LogConfig} is - rather
158         * than one per short lived object. A weak reference would risk silently dropping a
159         * listener (a lambda with no other strong reference could be collected almost
160         * immediately) which is the wrong failure mode for something whose entire job is not
161         * losing alerts. Call {@link AutoCloseable#close()} on the returned registration to
162         * unregister deterministically once the caller's own lifecycle ends.
163         * @param listener listener to register.
164         * @return registration; {@link AutoCloseable#close()} unregisters the listener.
165         */
166        public AutoCloseable addListener(Listener listener);
167
168        /**
169         * Notified of alerts as they happen. See {@link #addListener(Listener)}.
170         */
171        @FunctionalInterface
172        interface Listener {
173
174                /**
175                 * Called synchronously every time an alert is recorded. Should not throw -
176                 * exceptions are caught and reported separately so a broken listener cannot
177                 * disrupt alert recording or other listeners.
178                 * @param event the alert.
179                 */
180                void onAlert(LogEvent event);
181
182        }
183
184        /**
185         * Stats about alerts recorded.
186         *
187         * @param total total number of alerts ever recorded, including ones since evicted
188         * from the ring buffer.
189         * @param size number of alerts currently held in the ring buffer.
190         * @param capacity maximum number of alerts the ring buffer holds.
191         */
192        record Stats(long total, int size, int capacity) {
193        }
194
195        /**
196         * What building LogConfig and starting Rainbow Gum do with alerts recorded while
197         * starting, set by {@value LogProperties#ALERTS_FAIL_PROPERTY}. Checked once when
198         * {@link LogConfig} is built and once right after Rainbow Gum starts; alerts after
199         * that never fail anything. Evicting or clearing an alert from the diagnostic queue
200         * does not prevent it from failing startup.
201         */
202        enum FailLevel {
203
204                /**
205                 * Alerts never fail startup.
206                 */
207                @EnumAlias("false")
208                OFF,
209                /**
210                 * Default. Fail if a warning or error alert about configuration is recorded while
211                 * starting, such as a property key that was probably misspelled. Problems while
212                 * logging, such as an appender failing to write, do not fail startup.
213                 * @see LogAlerts#CONFIG_KEY
214                 */
215                CONFIG,
216                /**
217                 * Fail if any error alert is recorded while starting.
218                 */
219                ERROR,
220                /**
221                 * Fail if any warning or error alert is recorded while starting.
222                 */
223                @EnumAlias({ "true", "warn" })
224                WARNING;
225
226                static FailLevel parse(String value) {
227                        return switch (value.toLowerCase(java.util.Locale.ROOT)) {
228                                case "true", "warn" -> WARNING;
229                                case "false" -> OFF;
230                                default -> LogProperty.enumValue(FailLevel.class, value, "true", "false", "warn");
231                        };
232                }
233
234                boolean fails(LogEvent event) {
235                        return fails(event.level(), DefaultLogAlerts.isConfig(event));
236                }
237
238                boolean fails(Level level, boolean config) {
239                        boolean warningOrAbove = level == Level.ERROR || level == Level.WARNING;
240                        return switch (this) {
241                                case OFF -> false;
242                                case CONFIG -> config && warningOrAbove;
243                                case ERROR -> level == Level.ERROR;
244                                case WARNING -> warningOrAbove;
245                        };
246                }
247
248                /*
249                 * How a failure names what it failed on.
250                 */
251                String failing() {
252                        return switch (this) {
253                                case CONFIG -> "configuration alert(s) at warning";
254                                case OFF, ERROR, WARNING -> "alert(s) at " + name().toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT);
255                        };
256                }
257
258        }
259
260        /**
261         * The alert level for a property key that was set but not read while starting, set by
262         * {@value LogProperties#ALERTS_UNUSED_KEY_PROPERTY}. Keys are only checked in the
263         * debug modes that report them and when {@value LogProperties#ALERTS_FAIL_PROPERTY}
264         * would fail on them.
265         */
266        enum UnusedKeyLevel {
267
268                /**
269                 * Default. A key close to a key that was read is a warning with a suggestion, as
270                 * is a URI query parameter the component its URI chose does not read. Any other
271                 * unread key is information, since it may be for a component that was not chosen,
272                 * as is a key that differs from the suggestion only in a component's name or
273                 * type.
274                 */
275                INFO,
276                /**
277                 * Every unread key is a warning, so the default
278                 * {@code logging.alerts.fail=config} fails on any of them.
279                 */
280                @EnumAlias("warn")
281                WARNING,
282                /**
283                 * Every unread key is an error, so {@code logging.alerts.fail=error} fails on any
284                 * of them.
285                 */
286                ERROR;
287
288                static UnusedKeyLevel parse(String value) {
289                        return switch (value.toLowerCase(java.util.Locale.ROOT)) {
290                                case "warn" -> WARNING;
291                                default -> LogProperty.enumValue(UnusedKeyLevel.class, value, "warn");
292                        };
293                }
294
295                Level level(boolean likelyMistake) {
296                        return switch (this) {
297                                case INFO -> likelyMistake ? Level.WARNING : Level.INFO;
298                                case WARNING -> Level.WARNING;
299                                case ERROR -> Level.ERROR;
300                        };
301                }
302
303        }
304
305        /**
306         * What {@link #start(LogConfig)} does if, at that moment, at least one error alert
307         * has been recorded and still zero {@link Listener}s are registered - the situation
308         * Logback's {@code StatusManager} calls an unobserved status: nothing is watching, so
309         * whatever went wrong during property loading or a
310         * {@link io.jstach.rainbowgum.spi.RainbowGumServiceProvider.Configurator} would
311         * otherwise only ever have reached the individual, easy to miss stderr lines each
312         * {@link #alert(LogEvent)} call already produces.
313         * <p>
314         * Deliberately keyed as
315         * {@value LogProperties#ALERTS_UNOBSERVED_ERRORS_ACTION_PROPERTY} (an enum, not a
316         * boolean) since "fail" without "dump" first would throw away the only diagnostic
317         * evidence of why it failed.
318         */
319        enum UnobservedErrorsAction {
320
321                /**
322                 * Do nothing beyond the immediate reporting of warning and error events.
323                 */
324                NONE,
325                /**
326                 * Default. Report the whole backlog to {@code MetaLog} as one clearly labeled
327                 * block, the same way Logback auto-installs a console listener and prints its
328                 * accumulated status if nothing else is watching by the end of configuration -
329                 * RainbowGum still starts.
330                 */
331                DUMP,
332                /**
333                 * Same reporting as {@link #DUMP}, but then throws, so
334                 * {@link LogConfig.Builder#build()} (and therefore whatever is building a
335                 * {@link RainbowGum} from it) never completes. Goes further than Logback ever
336                 * does - an explicit, opt-in choice of integrity over resilience for deployments
337                 * where a silently-broken bootstrap is worse than refusing to start.
338                 */
339                FAIL;
340
341                static UnobservedErrorsAction parse(String value) {
342                        return LogProperty.enumValue(UnobservedErrorsAction.class, value);
343                }
344
345        }
346
347}
348
349/*
350 * Handed to PropertiesProviders. Buffers alerts until the configured LogAlerts exists,
351 * then drainTo replays the buffer into it and forwards every later call, so a provider
352 * may keep this instance and alert after provideProperties returns. Replay and swap
353 * happen under one lock so a concurrent alert is neither lost nor reordered. Listener
354 * registration is never supported: providers record alerts but cannot observe them.
355 */
356final class SwappableLogAlerts implements LogAlerts {
357
358        private final List<LogEvent> events = new ArrayList<>();
359
360        private long total;
361
362        private volatile @Nullable LogAlerts delegate;
363
364        @Override
365        public void alert(LogEvent event) {
366                var d = delegate;
367                if (d == null) {
368                        synchronized (this) {
369                                d = delegate;
370                                if (d == null) {
371                                        events.add(event.freeze());
372                                        total++;
373                                        return;
374                                }
375                        }
376                }
377                d.alert(event);
378        }
379
380        synchronized void drainTo(LogAlerts target) {
381                if (delegate != null) {
382                        throw new IllegalStateException("Alerts have already been drained");
383                }
384                for (var event : events) {
385                        target.alert(event);
386                }
387                events.clear();
388                delegate = target;
389        }
390
391        @Override
392        public synchronized List<LogEvent> dump() {
393                var d = delegate;
394                return d != null ? d.dump() : List.copyOf(events);
395        }
396
397        @Override
398        public synchronized void clear() {
399                var d = delegate;
400                if (d != null) {
401                        d.clear();
402                }
403                else {
404                        events.clear();
405                }
406        }
407
408        @Override
409        public synchronized Stats stats() {
410                var d = delegate;
411                return d != null ? d.stats() : new Stats(total, events.size(), Integer.MAX_VALUE);
412        }
413
414        @Override
415        public AutoCloseable addListener(Listener listener) {
416                throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Properties providers cannot register alert listeners");
417        }
418
419        @Override
420        public void start(LogConfig config) {
421                throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Properties provider alerts cannot be started");
422        }
423
424        @Override
425        public synchronized void close() {
426                // The drained delegate belongs to LogConfig, so only an undrained buffer is
427                // dropped.
428                if (delegate == null) {
429                        events.clear();
430                }
431        }
432
433}
434
435final class DefaultLogAlerts implements LogAlerts {
436
437        /*
438         * Used when neither the property nor the builder sets the fail level. LogConfig uses
439         * it too, to decide whether to record property reads.
440         */
441        static final FailLevel DEFAULT_FAIL_LEVEL = FailLevel.CONFIG;
442
443        static KeyValues configKeyValues() {
444                return KeyValues.of(Map.of(CONFIG_KEY, "true"));
445        }
446
447        static boolean isConfig(LogEvent event) {
448                return "true".equals(event.keyValues().getValueOrNull(CONFIG_KEY));
449        }
450
451        private final LogEvent[] ring;
452
453        private int start = 0;
454
455        private int size = 0;
456
457        private final AtomicLong total = new AtomicLong();
458
459        private final AtomicLong errors = new AtomicLong();
460
461        private final ReentrantLock lock = new ReentrantLock();
462
463        private final CopyOnWriteArrayList<Listener> listeners = new CopyOnWriteArrayList<>();
464
465        /*
466         * Kept apart from listeners.isEmpty() deliberately: DefaultLogConfig's own
467         * metrics-bridge listener (see its constructor) is always registered before
468         * start(...) ever runs, and a passive in-process counter nobody has wired an exporter
469         * to is not "someone is watching" in the sense UnobservedErrorsAction cares about -
470         * only a real addListener(Listener) call (this class's public API) flips this.
471         */
472        private volatile boolean hasExternalListener = false;
473
474        private final LogEventFactory eventFactory = LogEventFactory.of(DefaultLogAlerts.class.getName());
475
476        /*
477         * Resolved once, at construction (same as capacity) rather than inside start(...):
478         * unlike capacity this does not shape any constructor-time state, but LogProperties
479         * is available just as early, and start(LogConfig) is really about announcing "I have
480         * started" (config is there because a few edge cases needed it, not because this
481         * needed to be a start-time lookup).
482         */
483        private final UnobservedErrorsAction unobservedErrorsAction;
484
485        /*
486         * Private and deliberately not defensive - of(LogProperties) below is the only
487         * caller, and it has already validated both fields (capacity > 0, a resolvable
488         * UnobservedErrorsAction) before ever reaching this constructor. Re-checking here
489         * would be defensive programming duplicating what was already a real, reported
490         * validation failure one call up - see of(...)'s own comment.
491         */
492        private final FailLevel failLevel;
493
494        /*
495         * Names what set the fail level, for the failure message: the property, or
496         * logging.debug=help raising it.
497         */
498        private final String failLevelSource;
499
500        private final UnusedKeyLevel unusedKeyLevel;
501
502        /*
503         * Startup failure is independent of the bounded diagnostic queue. Keep the first
504         * failure and the count until startup ends, even if clear() or eviction removes it
505         * from the queue. All three fields are protected by lock.
506         */
507        private long startupFailures;
508
509        private @Nullable LogEvent firstStartupFailure;
510
511        private boolean startupComplete;
512
513        private DefaultLogAlerts(int capacity, UnobservedErrorsAction unobservedErrorsAction, FailLevel failLevel,
514                        String failLevelSource, UnusedKeyLevel unusedKeyLevel) {
515                this.ring = new LogEvent[capacity];
516                this.unobservedErrorsAction = unobservedErrorsAction;
517                this.failLevel = failLevel;
518                this.failLevelSource = failLevelSource;
519                this.unusedKeyLevel = unusedKeyLevel;
520        }
521
522        FailLevel failLevel() {
523                return failLevel;
524        }
525
526        UnusedKeyLevel unusedKeyLevel() {
527                return unusedKeyLevel;
528        }
529
530        /*
531         * Checks the startup failure count and lists retained failing alerts, including the
532         * first failure even if it left the queue. Called when LogConfig is built and right
533         * after Rainbow Gum starts.
534         */
535        void failIfAlerted(String phase) {
536                checkStartup(phase, false);
537        }
538
539        void finishStartup() {
540                checkStartup("starting", true);
541        }
542
543        private void checkStartup(String phase, boolean complete) {
544                lock.lock();
545                try {
546                        if (startupComplete) {
547                                return;
548                        }
549                        startupComplete = complete;
550                        var first = firstStartupFailure;
551                        if (first == null) {
552                                return;
553                        }
554                        var failing = new ArrayList<>(dump().stream().filter(failLevel::fails).toList());
555                        if (!failing.contains(first)) {
556                                failing.addFirst(first);
557                        }
558                        var sb = new StringBuilder();
559                        sb.append(startupFailures)
560                                .append(" ")
561                                .append(failLevel.failing())
562                                .append(" or above were recorded while ")
563                                .append(phase)
564                                .append(" and ")
565                                .append(failLevelSource)
566                                .append(":");
567                        for (var e : failing) {
568                                sb.append("\n[").append(e.level()).append("] ");
569                                e.formattedMessage(sb);
570                        }
571                        if (startupFailures > failing.size()) {
572                                sb.append("\n")
573                                        .append(startupFailures - failing.size())
574                                        .append(" additional failing alert(s) are no longer retained.");
575                        }
576                        throw new IllegalStateException(sb.toString());
577                }
578                finally {
579                        if (complete) {
580                                firstStartupFailure = null;
581                        }
582                        lock.unlock();
583                }
584        }
585
586        /*
587         * The fail level as resolved from properties, before LogAlerts exists, so LogConfig
588         * can decide whether to record property reads. Resolved again, and validated, by
589         * of(...).
590         */
591        static FailLevel failLevelOr(LogProperties properties, FailLevel fallback) {
592                var value = properties.valueOrNull(LogProperties.ALERTS_FAIL_PROPERTY);
593                try {
594                        return value == null ? fallback : FailLevel.parse(value);
595                }
596                catch (RuntimeException e) {
597                        return fallback;
598                }
599        }
600
601        /*
602         * The unused key level as resolved from properties, before LogAlerts exists, like
603         * failLevelOr. An invalid value is reported by of(...).
604         */
605        static UnusedKeyLevel unusedKeyLevelOr(LogProperties properties, UnusedKeyLevel fallback) {
606                var value = properties.valueOrNull(LogProperties.ALERTS_UNUSED_KEY_PROPERTY);
607                try {
608                        return value == null ? fallback : UnusedKeyLevel.parse(value);
609                }
610                catch (RuntimeException e) {
611                        return fallback;
612                }
613        }
614
615        /*
616         * Package-friend static factory: resolves and validates both
617         * LogProperties#ALERTS_CAPACITY_PROPERTY and
618         * LogProperties#ALERTS_UNOBSERVED_ERRORS_ACTION_PROPERTY against one shared Validator
619         * - a mistake in both at once is reported together instead of only the first one
620         * found - then constructs. requirePositiveCapacity is a plain int -> int validating
621         * transform (not an object construction) specifically so it can sit inside map(...)
622         * without tripping CheckerFramework's Initialization Checker, which does not refine a
623         * `new Foo(...)` expression back to @Initialized when it appears directly inside a
624         * lambda body passed through a generic method like map(...) - the one and only `new
625         * DefaultLogAlerts(...)` call stays a plain, unconditional statement here instead.
626         */
627        static DefaultLogAlerts of(LogProperties properties, @Nullable FailLevel failLevelFallback,
628                        UnusedKeyLevel unusedKeyLevelFallback, boolean help) {
629                var validator = LogProperty.Validator.of(LogAlerts.class);
630                var failLevelResult = properties.forKey(LogProperties.ALERTS_FAIL_PROPERTY)
631                        .ofString()
632                        .map(FailLevel::parse)
633                        .or(Objects.requireNonNullElse(failLevelFallback, DEFAULT_FAIL_LEVEL))
634                        .validateIfError(validator);
635                var unobservedErrorsActionResult = properties.forKey(LogProperties.ALERTS_UNOBSERVED_ERRORS_ACTION_PROPERTY)
636                        .ofString()
637                        .map(UnobservedErrorsAction::parse)
638                        .or(UnobservedErrorsAction.DUMP)
639                        .validateIfError(validator);
640                var unusedKeyLevelResult = properties.forKey(LogProperties.ALERTS_UNUSED_KEY_PROPERTY)
641                        .ofString()
642                        .map(UnusedKeyLevel::parse)
643                        .or(unusedKeyLevelFallback)
644                        .validateIfError(validator);
645                var capacityResult = properties.forKey(LogProperties.ALERTS_CAPACITY_PROPERTY)
646                        .ofInt()
647                        .or(LogAlerts.DEFAULT_CAPACITY)
648                        .map(DefaultLogAlerts::requirePositiveCapacity)
649                        .validateIfError(validator);
650                validator.validate();
651                var failLevel = failLevelResult.value();
652                String failLevelSource = LogProperties.ALERTS_FAIL_PROPERTY + "=" + failLevel.name().toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT);
653                boolean defaulted = failLevelFallback == null
654                                && properties.valueOrNull(LogProperties.ALERTS_FAIL_PROPERTY) == null;
655                if (help && (defaulted || failLevel != FailLevel.WARNING)) {
656                        failLevel = FailLevel.WARNING;
657                        failLevelSource = "logging.debug=help";
658                }
659                else if (defaulted) {
660                        failLevelSource += " (the default)";
661                }
662                return new DefaultLogAlerts(capacityResult.value(), unobservedErrorsActionResult.value(), failLevel,
663                                failLevelSource, unusedKeyLevelResult.value());
664        }
665
666        private static int requirePositiveCapacity(int capacity) {
667                if (capacity <= 0) {
668                        throw new IllegalArgumentException("capacity should be greater than 0");
669                }
670                return capacity;
671        }
672
673        @Override
674        public void alert(LogEvent event) {
675                var frozen = event.freeze();
676                total.incrementAndGet();
677                if (frozen.level() == Level.ERROR) {
678                        errors.incrementAndGet();
679                }
680                lock.lock();
681                try {
682                        if (!startupComplete && failLevel.fails(frozen)) {
683                                startupFailures++;
684                                if (firstStartupFailure == null) {
685                                        firstStartupFailure = frozen;
686                                }
687                        }
688                        if (size < ring.length) {
689                                ring[(start + size) % ring.length] = frozen;
690                                size++;
691                        }
692                        else {
693                                ring[start] = frozen;
694                                start = (start + 1) % ring.length;
695                        }
696                }
697                finally {
698                        lock.unlock();
699                }
700                for (var listener : listeners) {
701                        try {
702                                listener.onAlert(frozen);
703                        }
704                        catch (Exception e) {
705                                MetaLog.INSTANCE.log(eventFactory.eventNoArg(Level.ERROR, "LogAlerts.Listener threw", e));
706                        }
707                }
708                if (frozen.level() == Level.WARNING || frozen.level() == Level.ERROR) {
709                        MetaLog.INSTANCE.log(frozen);
710                }
711        }
712
713        @Override
714        public AutoCloseable addListener(Listener listener) {
715                listeners.add(listener);
716                hasExternalListener = true;
717                return () -> listeners.remove(listener);
718        }
719
720        /*
721         * DefaultLogConfig's own metrics-bridge listener goes through this instead of
722         * addListener(Listener) - see hasExternalListener's own comment for why.
723         */
724        void addInternalListener(Listener listener) {
725                listeners.add(listener);
726        }
727
728        @Override
729        public void start(LogConfig config) {
730                if (unobservedErrorsAction == UnobservedErrorsAction.NONE || hasExternalListener || errors.get() == 0) {
731                        return;
732                }
733                var backlog = dump();
734                MetaLog.error(eventFactory.eventNoArg(Level.ERROR,
735                                backlog.size() + " alert(s) were recorded before any LogAlerts.Listener was registered - "
736                                                + "dumping the backlog now since nothing else will see it:",
737                                null));
738                for (var event : backlog) {
739                        MetaLog.error(event);
740                }
741                if (unobservedErrorsAction == UnobservedErrorsAction.FAIL) {
742                        throw new IllegalStateException(
743                                        backlog.size() + " alert(s) were recorded before any LogAlerts.Listener was registered and "
744                                                        + LogProperties.ALERTS_UNOBSERVED_ERRORS_ACTION_PROPERTY + "=FAIL - refusing to start.");
745                }
746        }
747
748        @Override
749        public void close() {
750                listeners.clear();
751                lock.lock();
752                try {
753                        startupComplete = true;
754                        firstStartupFailure = null;
755                }
756                finally {
757                        lock.unlock();
758                }
759        }
760
761        @Override
762        public List<LogEvent> dump() {
763                lock.lock();
764                try {
765                        List<LogEvent> list = new ArrayList<>(size);
766                        for (int i = 0; i < size; i++) {
767                                var e = ring[(start + i) % ring.length];
768                                if (e != null) {
769                                        list.add(e);
770                                }
771                        }
772                        return List.copyOf(list);
773                }
774                finally {
775                        lock.unlock();
776                }
777        }
778
779        @Override
780        public void clear() {
781                lock.lock();
782                try {
783                        Arrays.fill(ring, null);
784                        start = 0;
785                        size = 0;
786                }
787                finally {
788                        lock.unlock();
789                }
790        }
791
792        @Override
793        public Stats stats() {
794                lock.lock();
795                try {
796                        return new Stats(total.get(), size, ring.length);
797                }
798                finally {
799                        lock.unlock();
800                }
801        }
802
803}
804
805/**
806 * Logging about logging. This is the static, always-available entry point used by code
807 * that cannot easily reach a {@link LogConfig} (e.g. before a {@link RainbowGum} is
808 * bound), and always reports directly (currently to stderr) rather than forwarding to a
809 * bound {@link RainbowGum}'s {@link LogConfig#alerts()} - alerts is a small bounded ring
810 * buffer meant to hold a curated, recent view of noteworthy logging-system problems, and
811 * {@link MetaLog} is used from enough different low level failure paths that routing it
812 * there risked flooding/evicting genuine alerts with whatever volume of things end up
813 * calling this class.
814 * <p>
815 * Components that already have (or can easily capture) a {@link LogConfig} - for example
816 * via {@link LogProvider} or {@link LogLifecycle#start(LogConfig)} - should prefer
817 * {@link LogConfig#alerts()} directly instead of this class.
818 *
819 * @author agentgt
820 */
821@SuppressWarnings("ImmutableEnumChecker")
822enum MetaLog implements LogEventLogger {
823
824        INSTANCE;
825
826        static Supplier<? extends @Nullable PrintStream> output = () -> System.err;
827
828        private final LogFormatter formatter = LogFormatter.builder() //
829                .text("[")
830                .level()
831                .text("] - RAINBOW_GUM")
832                .text(" - ")
833                .add(LogFormatter.of((b, e) -> {
834                        b.append(gumLoggerName(e.loggerName()));
835                }))
836                .text(" - ")
837                .message()
838                .textIfThrowable(" ")
839                .throwable((b, t) -> {
840                        int start = b.length();
841                        try {
842                                LogFormatter.ThrowableFormatter.appendThrowable(b, t);
843                        }
844                        catch (Throwable failure) {
845                                if (failure instanceof VirtualMachineError fatal && !(failure instanceof StackOverflowError)) {
846                                        throw fatal;
847                                }
848                                // A formatting failure can retain the broken event throwable as its
849                                // cause. Do not invoke either throwable again to report that failure.
850                                b.setLength(start);
851                                b.append(t.getClass().getName())
852                                        .append(" [stack trace unavailable: ")
853                                        .append(failure.getClass().getName())
854                                        .append("]");
855                        }
856                })
857                .newline()
858                .build();
859
860        /**
861         * Reports a logging system event at its original level.
862         * @param event event to log.
863         */
864        static void error(LogEvent event) {
865                INSTANCE.log(event);
866        }
867
868        /**
869         * Logs an error in the logging system.
870         * @param loggerName derived from class.
871         * @param throwable error to log.
872         */
873        static void error(Class<?> loggerName, Throwable throwable) {
874                String m = Objects.requireNonNullElse(throwable.getMessage(), "exception");
875                error(loggerName, m, throwable);
876        }
877
878        /**
879         * Logs an error in the logging system.
880         * @param loggerName derived from class.
881         * @param message error message.
882         * @param throwable error to log.
883         */
884        static void error(Class<?> loggerName, String message, Throwable throwable) {
885                var currentThread = Thread.currentThread();
886                var event = LogEvent.of(Instant.now(), currentThread.getName(), currentThread.threadId(), Level.ERROR,
887                                loggerName.getName(), message, KeyValues.of(), throwable);
888                error(event);
889        }
890
891        private static String gumLoggerName(String value) {
892                String prefix = "io.jstach.rainbowgum.";
893                if (value.startsWith(prefix)) {
894                        value = value.substring(prefix.length());
895                }
896                return value;
897        }
898
899        @Override
900        public void log(LogEvent event) {
901                var err = output.get();
902                if (err != null) {
903                        var sb = new StringBuilder();
904                        formatter.format(sb, event);
905                        err.append(sb);
906                }
907        }
908
909}
